Reggie Burrows Hodges (b. 1965, Compton) is known for his sensuous black and jewel-toned paintings of labor, community rituals, and solitary moments. His paintings combine observations of contemporary life with traditional artist techniques that date back centuries to the Renaissance era.

Hodges’s art is presented simultaneously in three venues in Los Angeles: CAAM, Art + Practice, and the Getty Center. In CAAM’s exhibition, *A Theater of Miracles*, Hodges’s compositions reflect the influence that Old Master paintings have had on his practice. His modern takes bring attention to everyday gestures while maintaining the sense of drama in the historical works. Several paintings are inspired by works in the Getty’s collection, including *The Miracle of the Quail* (1554) by Jacopo Bassano, which joins Hodges’s work on display at CAAM.

[Exhibitions > CAAM AT A+P]

The California African American Museum at A+P is a five-year collaboration (2022-2027) that brings CAAM organized shows to A+P’s exhibition space, and develops a hub for CAAM to incubate new programming. In return, A+P dedicates financial and staff resources to CAAM’s vision in support of the museum’s residency in Leimert Park. Our current exhibition *Giving you the best that I got* is on view October 11, 2025 – March 7, 2026.
